title: Mr. Drury, Latin and the valedictorian speech
summary: Teacher Mr. Drury unexpectedly teaches Latin, steadies the class, and patiently helps Thomas write his valedictorian speech.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And I was privileged to be valedictorian, which I didn't know what valedictorian was... But we had an English from Columbia, Mr. Drury. So we had had our first year of Latin in the Freshman class, but we didn't take it no more. And we got up to the Senior Class, and Mr. Drury come and told us that you got to have two years of a foreign language. In those days Latin was a foreign language. Nowadays, They got the Spanish and French and German and all that. So who would go teach us but Mr. Drury?! And Milt, he had to discern that we wondered what was he doing teaching us Latin. Because he was an English teacher! And after about the third or fourth day, he straightened us out. He let us understand that he had studied Latin, German, French and Italian -- he had about six or seven languages! We didn't say nothin' else about it. We let Mr. Drury take charge!
And he was so wonderful to us, because he knew that we didn't remember all that first grade of Latin from the
Freshman to the Senior class. And that way, he didn't rush us through, you know. But he told us one thing. He said, "If you get Latin, you'll have English." And it's so true. He was wonderful.
He was right. And all the other languages.

Right. And then another thing that he did for me... Here I am, valedictorian. So evidently, he knew that I didn't know too much about being a valedictorian. At first I didn't know what a valedictorian was. I found later that I was the one that had the highest grade from the Freshman to the Senior class in the same class. Because one boy had higher grades than me, but he had missed one year out, and he came in on our class. But originally, he was supposed to be a class ahead of us. Ralph Waller. So Mr. Drury patiently would sit down with me and helped me write my Valedictorian speech.
